key_insight: Deep learning on trial-level auditory oddball ERP waveforms classified schizophrenia vs healthy controls better than classical models using summary ERP features.
clinical_relevance: If validated, this approach could help develop more objective electrophysiology-based tools to support individual-level psychiatric classification and biomarker research.
method: 258 patients with schizophrenia and 142 healthy controls were studied.
EEG from an auditory duration oddball task was converted into trial-level mismatch ERP waveforms (-100 to 500 ms).
Five deep learning models were compared with classical machine learning on 18 ERP summary features, with demographic residualization fit only on training data.
evidence_signal: On the held-out test set, deep learning reached AUROC 0.797-0.857, outperforming classical feature-based models at 0.705-0.720.
watch_item: Performance was based on a single participant-level split, so broader validation across independent sites and recordings is still needed.
paper_title: Deep Learning for Individual-Level Classification of Schizophrenia Versus Healthy Controls from Trial-Level Auditory Oddball ERP Waveforms
